newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strikes disrupt French airlines, hospitals.
newsitem.headline: Strikes disrupt French airlines, hospitals.

text.p: Strike action forced TAT and Air Liberte, French units of British Airways, to cancel about 50 percent of their flights on Monday, a spokesman for the airlines said.
Cockpit crews at the airlines were in the sixth day of a stoppage over pay and conditions they say will be damaged by a merger of the two airlines.

A spokesman for the companies said the level of disruption was about the same as over the weekend while a union representative said that only 10 or 12 of 180 scheduled flights were guaranteed on Monday.

Meanwhile striking junior hospital doctors, ending their fifth week of a strike against goverment plans to cap health spending, vowed to keep up their protests and demanded wide-ranging negotiations with the government.
The strikers want the government to delay or scrap plans to fine doctors if the region in which they work overshoots pre-set spending limits, regardless of individual practice.
The government has refused to do away with the fines, but has made them more individualised and established a seven-year moratorium for new doctors setting up a practice.
The junior hospital doctors are supported by unions representing specialists in private practice who have opposed the government's reforms since they were announced in late 1995.
The strike has had only limited impact on the daily life of French people, but has provoked calls for a national debate on the state of French health care.
On Monday, the opposition Socialists said they were in favour of a parliamentary debate on the future of the public health system to help bring an end to the nagging strike.
